weaponConfig.summary: Weapons: Axe and Great Axe are the eligible weapon-skill families. Your core loop works from Lv. 10 without requiring weapon-skill talents or a specific subjob.

souls.equipmentCompatibility: Weapons: Axe and Great Axe are the eligible weapon-skill families. Your core loop works from Lv. 10 without requiring weapon-skill talents or a specific subjob.
souls.resourceSystem: Lv. 10 Core Loop: Call Packmate, Set Quarry, Pack Rend, and Raking Kick form a complete master-and-companion rhythm right away.
mechanics: Master-to-Hare TP Link: Landing Pack Rend or eligible Axe / Great Axe weapon skills on your shared quarry transfers TP to your hare. The transfer scales up as you level.
Hare-to-Master TP Link: When your hare lands Raking Kick on your shared quarry, it transfers TP back to you, also scaling up with level.
Independent 8-second cooldowns: Each direction of the TP link has its own 8-second recovery. Triggering a transfer to your hare does not lock out receiving TP back from Raking Kick, and vice versa.
Qualifying hits only: Misses, fully absorbed strikes, attacks on defeated enemies, and hits on a different target from your hare do not trigger the TP link.
Ready charges: Raking Kick spends standard Ready charges; track both Ready availability and the 8-second link timer so you do not waste a charge right before the link refreshes.
Lv. 30+ progression: Rally Packmate adds a separate summon recast at Lv. 30, and your hare's Attack, Accuracy, and Double Attack continue to improve as you gain levels.

souls.lore: A fierce pack-leader who stands shoulder-to-shoulder with a loyal guardian beast, sharing every hardship through an unbreakable bond.
souls.summary: Symbiotic one-handed Axe & Guardian Beast tank (Lv. 10+): always-on Soul-Link damage sharing with four zero-jug Guardian Beasts (Crab, Beetle, Tortoise, Tiger) at your level, Cure/overheal mirroring, and tank-reworked Ready skills.
souls.atAGlance: Alpha Warden is a symbiotic Beastmaster tank who holds the frontline alongside a loyal Guardian Beast. Through Soul-Link, your Guardian absorbs a major share of the damage directed at you, while its melee hits and Ready skills funnel enmity straight back to you. One-handed Axe weapon skills heal your Guardian and apply pressure to your target. Your Guardian does not tank in your place—you anchor the boss while your beast shares the punishment, brings tailored utility, and keeps you standing.
highlights: Growing Tank Passives: Master and Guardian Max HP, VIT, CHR, Defense, Damage Taken reduction, Enmity, Enmity Retention, Axe skill, and Guard/Parry rate scale steadily with level, alongside a 15s Ready recharge.

Zero-Jug Tank Beast Roster: Bestial Loyalty (5s recast) cycles Crab, Beetle, Tortoise, or Tiger out of combat; Call Beast (15s recast, usable in combat) summons your Guardian at your level; zero-biscuit Reward (25s recast) heals both you and your pet, cleanses 2 ailments, and grants a 12s hybrid Regen.

Soul-Link & Cure Mirroring: Always splits a major share of incoming master damage to your Guardian (pausing at critically low pet HP), funnels pet melee and Ready threat directly to you, and mirrors generous Cure, Waltz, Regen, and overheal recovery to your pet; 1H Axe weapon skills heal your pet and inflict Cripple.

Tank-Reworked Ready Skills: Grant heavy enmity, a burst of master TP, and Guardian utility (Crab: DEF/MDT/Stoneskin/Cripple/Breach; Beetle: Guard/Stun/Slow/Expose/Spoil; Tortoise: DT/Knockback Immunity/Stun/Breach/Accuracy Down; Tiger: Paralysis/Cripple/Pack TP/Heal).

Core Tank Cooldowns: Soul Bond (35s recast) equalizes master and pet HP percentages and grants Stoneskin; Feral Roar (25s recast) delivers an 8y AoE Stun, Slow, threat, and 1 Ready charge; enhanced Familiar grants 30s of strong mitigation, bonus HP, and full Ready charges.

weaponConfig.summary: Strict weapon loadout: Main-hand a one-handed Axe with nothing in your Sub slot—no shield, grip, or off-hand weapon. Equipping anything in Sub disables your core Guardian mechanics.

souls.equipmentCompatibility: Strict weapon loadout: Main-hand a one-handed Axe with nothing in your Sub slot—no shield, grip, or off-hand weapon. Equipping anything in Sub disables your core Guardian mechanics.
souls.resourceSystem: Growing Tank Passives: Master and Guardian Max HP, VIT, CHR, Defense, Damage Taken reduction, Enmity, Enmity Retention, Axe skill, and Guard/Parry rate scale steadily with level, alongside a 15s Ready recharge.
mechanics: Soul-Link: Always active while your Guardian is healthy, redirecting a major share of eligible incoming master damage to your pet. The link pauses if your Guardian falls to critically low HP.
Enmity Funneling: Your Guardian's melee attacks and Ready skills funnel their enmity directly to you so you remain the primary tank.
Guardian AoE Immunity: Your Guardians possess strong natural damage reduction and are immune to qualifying AoE and conal attacks. This protection applies to the pet, not to you.
Cure & Overheal Mirroring: Qualifying Cure, Waltz, and Regen healing received by you mirrors a substantial portion of both effective healing and overhealing directly onto your Guardian.

Zero-Jug Guardians & Zero-Biscuit Reward: Bestial Loyalty (5-second recast) cycles between Crab, Beetle, Tortoise, and Tiger; Call Beast (15-second recast, usable in combat) calls your selected Guardian at your level; Reward (25-second recast) heals both master and pet, cleanses 2 ailments, and applies a 12-second Regen without consuming biscuits.
One-Handed Axe Weapon Skills: Landing eligible one-handed Axe weapon skills heals your Guardian for a level-scaled share of its maximum HP and inflicts Cripple.

souls.lore: A keen naturalist of Vana’diel’s ecosystems who reads a creature’s lineage and guides companions toward its natural vulnerability.
souls.summary: Tactical physical-weakness support (Lv. 10+): study your quarry to reveal its physical vulnerability and command a mandragora tracker to expose it for your party's regular attacks.
souls.atAGlance: Wildsavant is a tactical physical-weakness support Soul that studies an enemy's anatomy and directs a mandragora tracker to pry open its defenses. Your job is to read the quarry, trigger a brief vulnerability window, and call out which physical damage type—blunt, piercing, or slashing—your party should exploit. Unlike a blanket attack buff, exposure specifically empowers matching ordinary physical hits.
highlights: Lv. 10 Opening Loop: Call Tracker, Track Quarry, Read Quarry (15y, 60s), and Expose Quarry enable targeted party support from the very first pull.
Targeted Exposure Window: Expose Quarry boosts up to 2 matching ordinary physical hits per party member (at most 1 claim per attack round) for 8s, extending to 10s at Lv. 50.
Family Knowledge Pays Off: Known monster families receive a stronger exposure bonus than unknown or tied families (which begin on blunt), with potency scaling up as you level.
Lv. 30 & Lv. 50 Mastery: Lv. 30 records the quarry's latest completed hostile action after a read; Lv. 50 unlocks Choose Weakness to cycle the next exposure's physical type.

weaponConfig.summary: Weapon: Axe is the eligible weapon-skill family. Your support toolkit works right away with standard gear, any subjob, and no weapon-skill talent requirements.

souls.equipmentCompatibility: Weapon: Axe is the eligible weapon-skill family. Your support toolkit works right away with standard gear, any subjob, and no weapon-skill talent requirements.
souls.resourceSystem: Targeted Exposure Window: Expose Quarry boosts up to 2 matching ordinary physical hits per party member (at most 1 claim per attack round) for 8s, extending to 10s at Lv. 50.
mechanics: Read Quarry: 15-yalm range, lasts 60 seconds. Identifies the quarry's physical weakness (known monster families receive a stronger exposure bonus than unknown families; unknown or tied targets start on blunt, which includes hand-to-hand).

Expose Quarry: Grants your mandragora 6 seconds to land a melee strike and open the exposure window. The window lasts 8 seconds at Lv. 10–49 and 10 seconds from Lv. 50 onward, with bonus strength growing as you level up.

Hit caps & eligible attacks: Each party member can benefit from at most 2 matching hits per exposure, limited to 1 claim per attack round. Only ordinary melee attacks and eligible single ranged shots qualify; weapon skills, skillchains, counterattacks, and multi-shot volleys do not trigger the bonus.
Lv. 30 Action Observation: After a read, records the quarry's most recent completed qualifying hostile action on your Soul HUD.
Lv. 50 Choose Weakness: Lets you select which physical damage type your next exposure will open, letting you adapt to your party's lineup.
Multiple Beastspeakers: When multiple exposures overlap on the same target, the stronger exposure takes precedence.

souls.lore: A dashing blade-dancer of the open road who weaves twin-steel flourishes into vibrant, echoing melodies.
souls.summary: Wandering troubadour melee DPS (Lv. 10+): dual-wield Daggers or Swords to build Cadence stacks, unleash Sonic weapon-skill follow-ups, and trigger Encore haste while keeping party songs intact.
souls.atAGlance: Skald is a dual-wielding Dagger and Sword melee Bard that preserves full party song utility while turning frontline uptime into Cadence. Landed melee hits and Lunge & Flourish build up to 5 Cadence stacks, which eligible weapon skills spend for a bonus light-elemental sonic strike and an Encore combat buff. You gain innate Dual Wield and growing melee stats, provided you fight with a Dagger or Sword in your main hand.
highlights: Growing Melee Passives: Unlocks Dual Wield and steadily scales DEX, CHR, Attack, Accuracy, Critical Hit rate, and Dual Wield speed as you level.

Cadence & Sonic Follow-Ups: Eligible Dagger and Sword hits build up to 5 Cadence stacks (boosting critical chance); eligible weapon skills spend them for a light sonic follow-up strike and a 12s Encore self-buff.

Burst & Song Synergy: Unlocks Lunge & Flourish (20s recast, 4y) and Troubadour's Encore (45s recast) without overwriting maintained party songs, with offensive payoffs scaling up to 4 active buff songs.

weaponConfig.summary: Dual one-handed wielding unlocked at Lv. 10 using Dagger and Sword pairings.

souls.equipmentCompatibility: Weapons: Main-hand a Dagger or Sword, and pair it with an appropriate off-hand weapon using your granted Dual Wield. Fighting with a different main-hand weapon disables your Cadence and Encore triggers.
souls.resourceSystem: Cadence & Sonic Follow-Ups: Eligible Dagger and Sword hits build up to 5 Cadence stacks (boosting critical chance); eligible weapon skills spend them for a light sonic follow-up strike and a 12s Encore self-buff.
mechanics: Cadence: Stacks up to 5, lasting roughly 20 seconds. Each stack increases your critical-hit rate. Built by eligible Dagger/Sword melee hits and Lunge & Flourish; spent by eligible Dagger/Sword weapon skills.
Lunge & Flourish: 20-second recast, 4-yalm range. Deals piercing damage scaled by up to 4 active buff songs, applies Defense Down if absent, grants 2 Cadence stacks, and awards a burst of TP.

Sonic Follow-Up & Encore: Spending Cadence with an eligible Dagger or Sword weapon skill unleashes a light-elemental sonic follow-up hit and activates Encore for 12 seconds, granting boosted Haste, Critical Hit rate, and Weapon Skill damage.

Troubadour's Encore: 45-second recast. Immediately grants 5 Cadence stacks (25-second duration) and an empowered 15-second Encore buff with stronger Haste, Critical Hit rate, and Weapon Skill damage, without overwriting your active songs.
Dual Wield & Passive Growth: Unlocks Dual Wield and steadily improves your DEX, CHR, Attack, Accuracy, Critical Hit rate, and Dual Wield delay reduction as you level up.
Weapon eligibility: Only Dagger and Sword main-hand melee hits and weapon skills trigger Cadence generation, Sonic follow-ups, and Encore.

souls.lore: A concert virtuoso of Vana’diel’s ancient harmonies whose dramatic crescendos both uplift companions and shatter foes with sound.
souls.summary: Tavnazian lyrical mage (Lv. 10+): transforms offensive Threnodies, Requiems, Elegies, and Finale into fast-casting elemental nukes that can Magic Burst and build Resonance.
souls.atAGlance: Cantor is a magical song nuker and burst-support Bard. Your offensive Threnody, Requiem, Elegy, and Magic Finale songs become fast-casting magical nukes that can Magic Burst and build Cantor's Resonance. Once you stack Resonance to 3, Grand Finale detonates your accumulated stacks and the target's active song debuffs in a heavy light-elemental burst. Best of all, your offensive songs never overwrite your party's maintained buff songs.
highlights: Magical Song Nukes: Threnodies, Requiems, Elegies, and Magic Finale deal CHR- and Magic Attack-scaled elemental damage, can Magic Burst, and build up to 3 stacks of Cantor's Resonance (30s).
Protected Party Support: Offensive songs never overwrite your maintained Ballad, Scherzo, or other party buff songs.

Burst Toolkit & Passives: Unlocks Grand Finale (20s recast, 20y Resonance detonation) and Lyrical Overdrive (45s recast, 15s burst window), alongside growing CHR, Magic Attack Bonus, Magic Accuracy, song skills, Fast Cast, and passive Refresh.

weaponConfig.summary: Equipment: Carry an appropriate instrument and gear focused on CHR, Singing and instrument skill, Magic Attack Bonus, and Magic Accuracy. You are not tied to any specific melee weapon.

souls.equipmentCompatibility: Equipment: Carry an appropriate instrument and gear focused on CHR, Singing and instrument skill, Magic Attack Bonus, and Magic Accuracy. You are not tied to any specific melee weapon.
souls.resourceSystem: Magical Song Nukes: Threnodies, Requiems, Elegies, and Magic Finale deal CHR- and Magic Attack-scaled elemental damage, can Magic Burst, and build up to 3 stacks of Cantor's Resonance (30s).
mechanics: Cantor's Resonance: Stacks up to 3 with a 30-second duration. Eligible offensive songs build stacks, and each active stack increases your Magic Attack Bonus.

Grand Finale: 20-second recast, 20-yalm range. Consumes all active Resonance stacks to unleash a single-target light-magic burst that scales with your consumed Resonance stacks and the number of active qualifying song debuffs (Threnody, Requiem, Elegy) on the target.
Lyrical Overdrive: 45-second recast, 15-second duration. Strongly boosts Magic Attack Bonus, Magic Accuracy, Fast Cast, offensive song damage, and Magic Burst potency while active.
Magic Burst Synergy: Both your offensive songs and Grand Finale can Magic Burst off compatible party skillchains.
Protected Party Buffs: Casting offensive debuff songs will not displace your maintained party buff songs.
Passive Progression: Your CHR, Magic Attack Bonus, Magic Accuracy, Singing and instrument skill, song cast speed, Fast Cast, and passive Refresh all scale upward as you level up.

souls.lore: A defiant troubadour whose resonant chords and iron-willed ballads command the attention of titans while fortifying their own spirit.
souls.summary: Classic song-enmity Bard tank (Lv. 10+): holds bosses through high-threat offensive songs, passively empowered Minne/Paeon/Scherzo defensive auras, and dedicated tank cooldowns.
souls.atAGlance: Provocateur is a song-enmity Bard tank, paying homage to classic level-75 Bard tanking. You anchor enemies through heavy-threat offensive and debuff songs while maintaining Minne, Paeon, and Scherzo for passive defensive power. Dissonant Chord gives you a ranged snap-taunt with Attack Down, while Iron Aria opens a sturdy defensive window with sonic reflect for heavy boss phases. Provocateur trades away personal damage output in exchange for reliable threat control and song-driven survivability.
highlights: Heavy Song Enmity: Lullaby, Elegy, Requiem, Threnody, and Magic Finale generate strong Volatile and Cumulative Enmity to lock down targets.

Passive Defensive Auras: Keeping Minne (extra physical mitigation), Paeon (stronger level-scaled Regen), and Scherzo (tank-buster dampening) active empowers your survivability without spamming recasts.

Tank Cooldowns & Growth: Unlocks Dissonant Chord (15s recast, 20y snap-taunt with Attack Down) and Iron Aria (45s recast, 15s mitigation and sonic reflect), with tank durability and song casting stability scaling upward with level.

weaponConfig.summary: Equipment: Equip a Shield, sturdy defensive armor, Damage Taken reduction, Max HP, CHR, and an appropriate instrument for smooth song casting. No specific main-hand weapon is required for your core threat loop.

souls.equipmentCompatibility: Equipment: Equip a Shield, sturdy defensive armor, Damage Taken reduction, Max HP, CHR, and an appropriate instrument for smooth song casting. No specific main-hand weapon is required for your core threat loop.
souls.resourceSystem: Dissonant Chord: 15-second recast, 20-yalm range. Generates heavy immediate and lasting enmity and applies Attack Down for 15 seconds if the enemy does not already suffer from it.
mechanics: Dissonant Chord: 15-second recast, 20-yalm range. Generates heavy immediate and lasting enmity and applies Attack Down for 15 seconds if the enemy does not already suffer from it.
Iron Aria: 45-second recast, 15-second duration. Grants strong physical and magical damage reduction, bonus Defense, extra Enmity, and sonic reflection while active.

Empowered Minne, Paeon & Scherzo: Keeping Minne active grants extra physical damage reduction; active Paeon provides stronger level-scaled Regen without repeated recasting; active Scherzo dampens severe single-hit tank-busters.
Song-Enmity Engine: Offensive and debuff songs (Lullaby, Elegy, Requiem, Threnody, Finale) generate heavy Volatile and Cumulative Enmity, scaling by song family.
Tank Tradeoff: Provocateur carries heavily reduced personal damage output in exchange for durable tank passives and potent song-based threat.
Passive Progression: Your tank survivability, defensive stats, interruption resistance, song casting speed, and passive song enhancements all strengthen as you level up.

souls.lore: A dead-eyed marksman of quiet patience who claims a clear sightline and lets a single, unerring shot speak across the horizon.
souls.summary: Deliberate single-target marksman (Lv. 10+): commit to a stationary aim with a Gun or Crossbow to unleash one high-precision, heavy-impact shot.
souls.atAGlance: Sniper is a deliberate single-target marksman Soul for Gun and Crossbow users. Sightline Shot trades a brief stationary aiming window for one high-precision, high-impact ranged strike. At Lv. 50, Deep Sight lets you commit to a slower 4-second aim for even heavier damage, or toggle back to the standard 3-second shot when the encounter demands mobility. Sniper rewards patience, clean sightlines, and decisive individual shots rather than rapid-fire volleys.
highlights: Sightline Shot (Lv. 10+): Fires one high-accuracy, heavy-damage projectile after a 3s aim (20y range, 12s recast), with accuracy and damage growing as you level.
Deep Sight (Lv. 50+): Toggle stance (5s recast) that trades a longer 4s aim for substantially heavier single-shot damage at high levels.
Forgiving Cancel Rules: Moving beyond 1y, losing your firing lane, changing your engaged target, or being incapacitated cancels aim without spending ammo and grants a 3s retry.
Growing Marksman Passives: Marksmanship skill, Ranged Accuracy, Ranged Attack, and AGI scale steadily as you level up.

weaponConfig.summary: Weapon and ammunition: Wield a Gun with bullets or a Crossbow with bolts, and pack plenty of matching ammo. Marksmanship is your eligible weapon-skill family, and even a basic Crossbow with bolts enables the full opening loop.

souls.equipmentCompatibility: Weapon and ammunition: Wield a Gun with bullets or a Crossbow with bolts, and pack plenty of matching ammo. Marksmanship is your eligible weapon-skill family, and even a basic Crossbow with bolts enables the full opening loop.
souls.resourceSystem: Deep Sight (Lv. 50+): Toggle stance (5s recast) that trades a longer 4s aim for substantially heavier single-shot damage at high levels.
mechanics: Sightline Shot (Lv. 10+): 12-second recast, 20-yalm range, 3-second aim. Fires one high-precision projectile with bonus Ranged Accuracy and strong single-target damage that scales upward as you level.
Deep Sight (Lv. 50+): Toggle ability on a 5-second recast. Extends Sightline Shot's aim to 4 seconds in exchange for much heavier single-shot damage, scaling further at high levels.
Aim-Break Rules: Moving more than 1 yalm, losing your firing lane, switching your engaged target, unequipping valid weapon/ammo, or suffering incapacitation cancels the aim.
Forgiving Cancel Recovery: Canceled aims spend no ammo and incur only a 3-second retry instead of the full 12-second recast.
Passive Progression: Your Marksmanship skill, Ranged Accuracy, Ranged Attack, and AGI all increase steadily as you gain levels.
Soul HUD: Tracks your active aim progress, standard vs. Deep Sight mode, and remaining Sightline Shot recast.

souls.lore: A frontier tracker bonded to a fierce wild companion, directing primal loyalty from the thick of the hunt to hold the wilderness at bay.
souls.summary: Modal beastmaster Ranger (Lv. 10+): bond with Glacial Tuskers (Wild Raaz / Cehuetzi) to anchor bosses as a pet tank, or Volcanic Saurians (Stalker Raptor / Gabbrath) to project an offensive party pack aura.
souls.atAGlance: Fangbound is a modal beastmaster Ranger whose active companion defines your combat role. Summoning a Glacial Tusker turns your beast into a dedicated single-target frontline tank that absorbs your threat and receives forwarded cures; summoning a Volcanic Saurian shifts you into an offensive pack-support Ranger who empowers nearby allies. You cannot run both roles at once—your active beast determines your stance, threat behavior, and party utility, making your companion choice and its shared 60-second summon recast your most important tactical decisions.
highlights: Primeval Pack Passives: Auto-equips a starter Crossbow and bolts at Lv. 10 if empty, grants full Ammo Recycle and zero ranged distance penalty, and scales Max HP, Archery/Marksmanship, Ranged Accuracy, Snapshot/Rapid Shot, and Store TP while a pet is active.
Warden's Ration: Eligible Archery and Marksmanship weapon skills heal your active beast for a scaling share of its Max HP and grant a surge of Pet TP.

Glacial Tusker Stance (Wild Raaz Lv. 10 / Cehuetzi Lv. 75): Dedicated pet-tank mode that trades away your personal damage for high pet Max HP, strong pet mitigation, AoE/conal immunity, heavy pet enmity, master-to-pet threat forwarding, and generous Cure/overheal forwarding.

Volcanic Saurian Stance (Stalker Raptor Lv. 10 / Gabbrath Lv. 75): Hybrid pack-support mode with reduced enmity and a 15y Party Pack Aura boosting allies' Accuracy, Ranged Accuracy, Attack, and Ranged Attack.
Single-Target Pet Commands: Rimetusk Gore (30s), Saurian Rend (30s), and Primeval Takedown (45s) deliver stance-tailored threat, sustain, TP, and burst payoffs.

weaponConfig.summary: Ranged loadout: Equip a Bow or Crossbow with matching arrows or bolts (if empty at Lv. 10, a starter Crossbow and bolts are auto-equipped). Fangbound enjoys full Ammo Recycle, no ranged distance damage penalty, and growing Archery/Marksmanship, Ranged Accuracy, Snapshot/Rapid Shot, and Store TP while a pet is active.

souls.equipmentCompatibility: Ranged loadout: Equip a Bow or Crossbow with matching arrows or bolts (if empty at Lv. 10, a starter Crossbow and bolts are auto-equipped). Fangbound enjoys full Ammo Recycle, no ranged distance damage penalty, and growing Archery/Marksmanship, Ranged Accuracy, Snapshot/Rapid Shot, and Store TP while a pet is active.
souls.resourceSystem: Primeval Pack Passives: Auto-equips a starter Crossbow and bolts at Lv. 10 if empty, grants full Ammo Recycle and zero ranged distance penalty, and scales Max HP, Archery/Marksmanship, Ranged Accuracy, Snapshot/Rapid Shot, and Store TP while a pet is active.
mechanics: Apex Bond (Modal Stances): Only one beast can be active at a time, and all beast summons share a 60-second recast.

Glacial Tusker (Wild Raaz Lv. 10 / Cehuetzi Lv. 75): Dedicated pet-tank stance. Heavily lowers your personal damage output in exchange for massive pet Max HP, strong pet damage reduction, immunity to qualifying AoE and conal attacks, heightened pet enmity, master-to-pet enmity forwarding, and generous Cure/overheal forwarding from master to pet.

Volcanic Saurian (Stalker Raptor Lv. 10 / Gabbrath Lv. 75): Hybrid offensive-support stance. Moderately trims personal damage and reduces enmity while projecting a 15-yalm Party Pack Aura that boosts allies' Accuracy, Ranged Accuracy, Attack, and Ranged Attack.
Warden's Ration: Landing an eligible Archery or Marksmanship weapon skill heals your active beast for a level-scaled share of its Max HP and grants it a strong burst of Pet TP.

Single-Target Pet Commands: Rimetusk Gore (30s recast, 20y) builds pet threat, heals the beast, and boosts its defense; Saurian Rend (30s recast, 20y) heals the beast and grants nearby allies TP and offensive buffs; Primeval Takedown (45s recast, 20y) adds threat, stun, and pet Stoneskin in Tusker mode, or high damage and master TP in Saurian mode.

Primeval Pack (Passive Growth): Grants Lv. 10 starter Crossbow/Bolt convenience, full Ammo Recycle, no ranged distance penalty, and steadily scaling Max HP, Archery/Marksmanship skill, Ranged Accuracy, Snapshot/Rapid Shot, and Store TP whenever a pet is active.

souls.lore: A mystic fletching artisan who inscribes elemental resonance onto every arrow, painting luminous marks for allies to awaken.
souls.summary: Coordinated elemental Bow support (Lv. 10+): attune your bow to one of six elements and land an arrow to amplify your party's next matching spell or skillchain.
souls.atAGlance: Spellfletcher is a coordinated elemental Bow support Soul. You attune your bow to one of six elements and fire Attunement Arrow to place an elemental mark on a quarry, amplifying the damage of your party's next matching direct spell or skillchain. Rather than acting as a passive ranged damage buff, Spellfletcher rewards communication and timing with your teammates. When adventuring solo, you can claim your own mark with a matching elemental Bow weapon skill at reduced strength.
highlights: Attunement Arrow (Lv. 10+): A landed Bow shot (20y, 16s recast) marks one enemy with Fire, Ice, Wind, Earth, Lightning, or Water; both duration (10s up to 14s) and damage boost grow with level.
Coordinated Party Payoff: The first matching direct elemental spell or skillchain from a party member consumes the mark for amplified damage.
Solo Self-Claim: While solo, you can claim your own mark with a matching elemental Bow weapon skill at reduced strength.
Mark Discipline: One live mark per Spellfletcher and per enemy; missed shots spend one arrow and trigger the 16s recast without replacing an existing mark.

weaponConfig.summary: Weapon: Equip a Bow and compatible arrows. Archery is your eligible weapon-skill family, and Attunement Arrow requires a landed Bow shot to apply its mark.

souls.equipmentCompatibility: Weapon: Equip a Bow and compatible arrows. Archery is your eligible weapon-skill family, and Attunement Arrow requires a landed Bow shot to apply its mark.
souls.resourceSystem: Coordinated Party Payoff: The first matching direct elemental spell or skillchain from a party member consumes the mark for amplified damage.
mechanics: Attunement Arrow (Lv. 10+): 16-second recast, 20-yalm range. Requires a Bow and arrows. A landed shot marks the quarry with your chosen element; the mark's duration (starting at 10 seconds and growing up to 14 seconds at high levels) and damage bonus both scale upward as you level up.
Six Selectable Elements: Cycle freely between Fire, Ice, Wind, Earth, Lightning, and Water using Next/Previous Attunement (1-second recast).

Eligible Party Claims: A party member's matching direct elemental spell or skillchain that deals positive damage consumes the mark for a notable damage boost. Periodic damage-over-time ticks and unrelated attacks do not trigger it.
Skillchain Element Resolution: For multi-element skillchains, the skillchain's actual resolved element must match your mark.
Solo Self-Claim: While solo, you can consume your own mark using a matching elemental Bow weapon skill for a reduced bonus.

Mark Limits: One active mark per Spellfletcher and one active mark per enemy. Only an eligible hit that actually deals damage consumes the mark; a missed Attunement Arrow leaves any existing mark untouched.

souls.lore: A wandering master of the great katana whose serene clarity absorbs terrible blows with stoic grace before shedding their weight.
souls.summary: Masterless Mushin tank: requires a Great Katana to unlock Seigan mitigation, multi-charge Mind's Eye counter-anticipation, and Mushin Stagger damage deferral purified by Tachi weapon skills, Meditate, and Blade Bash.
souls.atAGlance: Ronin is a Great Katana tank built around Seigan, Mind's Eye anticipation, and Mushin Stagger. Instead of absorbing every blow in full on impact, Ronin defers a portion of incoming damage into a temporary Stagger pool that ticks down over time. Landing timely Tachi weapon skills, Meditate, or Blade Bash purifies that pool—turning disciplined timing into durability, self-recovery, and steady threat. Playing Ronin well is all about planning your next purge before deferred damage catches up with you.
highlights: Open weapon choice, but requires a Great Katana for Ronin passives, Mushin Stagger, and job ability upgrades.
Unlocks Seigan, Third Eye (15s recast, 2-3 Mind's Eye charges), Meditate, and Blade Bash at Lv. 10+.
Mind's Eye anticipates melee swings and single-target enemy TP moves, countering with a Great Katana slash that restores TP and builds heavy enmity.
Mushin Poise defers part of incoming hit damage into a 9s Stagger pool that is purified by Tachi weapon skills, Blade Bash, and Meditate.
Warding Circle (120s recast) bolsters party damage mitigation and Magic Evasion; Meikyo Shisui grants strong personal mitigation, a full Stagger purge, and instant Mind's Eye.

weaponConfig.summary: Essential weapon: Main-hand a Great Katana. Although equipment rules remain open, Ronin's tank passives, Seigan stance upgrades, Mind's Eye counter-attacks, and Mushin Stagger require a Great Katana.

souls.equipmentCompatibility: Essential weapon: Main-hand a Great Katana. Although equipment rules remain open, Ronin's tank passives, Seigan stance upgrades, Mind's Eye counter-attacks, and Mushin Stagger require a Great Katana.
souls.resourceSystem: Unlocks Seigan, Third Eye (15s recast, 2-3 Mind's Eye charges), Meditate, and Blade Bash at Lv. 10+.
mechanics: Mushin Stagger: Defers part of qualifying incoming damage (more while in Seigan) into a capped Stagger pool that ticks down over three ticks across 9 seconds unless purified.
Stagger purification: Eligible Tachi weapon skills clear a major portion of your pending Stagger; Meditate, Blade Bash, and Meikyo Shisui completely purify the pool under their respective conditions.

Mind's Eye: Third Eye (15-second recast) grants two anticipation charges before Lv. 50 and three charges from Lv. 50 onward, countering eligible melee hits and single-target enemy TP moves for bonus TP and heavy enmity.
Seigan: Ronin's tank stance on a 15-second recast, providing damage mitigation, Defense, Counter rate, and enmity while wielding a Great Katana.
Blade Bash: 30-second recast at 4-yalm range; stuns, inflicts Attack Down, builds heavy enmity, and fully clears Stagger.

Meditate & emergency tools: Meditate provides a full Stagger purge, healing, and threat; Warding Circle shields the party; Meikyo Shisui grants strong temporary damage mitigation and instant Mind's Eye readiness.

souls.lore: A noble retainer of Far Eastern courtly arms who bridges distant bowcraft and drawing-blade mastery in a single unbroken cadence.
souls.summary: Tenzen-inspired Bow and Great Katana skirmisher: elevates Archery to A+ while preserving arrows without consuming them, auto-shoots up to 20y outside melee range, and weaves Tachi and Archery weapon skills via Drawn Oisoya and Cosmic Brand.
souls.atAGlance: Imperial Archer is a Bow-and-Great-Katana skirmisher inspired by Tenzen, built around weaving Archery and Tachi weapon skills back and forth. Each weapon family primes the other: Drawn Oisoya empowers your next Archery weapon skill, while Cosmic Brand supercharges your next Great Katana follow-up and its skillchain damage. Oisoya Shot opens the dance from range and can establish both primers at once. The goal is fluid hybrid pressure and sharp skillchain execution rather than camping a single weapon.
highlights: Open weapon choice; equipping a Bow grants A+ Archery skill, preserves arrows without consuming them, and strengthens Ranged Accuracy, Ranged Attack, and Snapshot.
Auto-attacks with a Bow up to 20y outside melee range with no point-blank penalty.
Oisoya Shot (25s recast, 20y): piercing arrow that restores TP, primes Chainbound on unchained targets, and grants Drawn Oisoya (plus Cosmic Brand with a Great Katana).
Tachi weapon skills grant Drawn Oisoya to empower your next Archery weapon skill and refund TP; Archery weapon skills grant Cosmic Brand to empower your next Tachi and its skillchain damage.
Hasso works with either a Bow or Great Katana (boosting Snapshot, Ranged Attack, Ranged Accuracy, AGI, and Ability Haste); Sengikori and Meikyo Shisui amplify Bow-and-Blade chains.

weaponConfig.summary: Weapons: Equip a Great Katana in Main and a Bow with arrows in Ranged/Ammo. You can auto-attack with your Bow up to 20 yalms away outside melee range with no point-blank penalty, and the full alternating loop requires both weapons.

souls.equipmentCompatibility: Weapons: Equip a Great Katana in Main and a Bow with arrows in Ranged/Ammo. You can auto-attack with your Bow up to 20 yalms away outside melee range with no point-blank penalty, and the full alternating loop requires both weapons.
souls.resourceSystem: Tachi weapon skills grant Drawn Oisoya to empower your next Archery weapon skill and refund TP; Archery weapon skills grant Cosmic Brand to empower your next Tachi and its skillchain damage.
mechanics: Oisoya Mastery: Elevates Archery to A+ skill, preserves arrows without consuming them, enables Bow auto-attacks up to 20 yalms outside melee range, removes point-blank Bow penalties, and powers the Drawn Oisoya / Cosmic Brand loop.
Drawn Oisoya: A 15-second primer empowering your next eligible Archery weapon skill, refunding TP, and granting Cosmic Brand.
Cosmic Brand: A 15-second primer empowering your next eligible Great Katana weapon skill and its skillchain damage, refunding TP, and granting Drawn Oisoya.
Oisoya Shot: 25-second recast, 20-yalm range (requires Bow); restores TP, primes a 10-second Chainbound window on unchained targets, and grants Drawn Oisoya (plus Cosmic Brand with a Great Katana).
Hasso (Bow & Blade): 30-second recast; enhances Snapshot, Ranged Attack, Ranged Accuracy, AGI, and Ability Haste even while wielding a Bow.

Level progression: Hasso's ranged bonuses, Oisoya Shot's TP return, primer strength, and skillchain synergy grow as you level. Sengikori unlocks at Lv. 30, and Konzen-ittai and Shikikoyo unlock at Lv. 50.

souls.lore: A commanding shogunate champion whose decisive bladework kindles an inspiring martial aura across every warrior at their side.
souls.summary: Cursed Onimaru and Iaijutsu battlefield support (Lv. 10+): pairs an aggressive Great Katana and 20s Hagakure sheathe-and-draw rhythm with Ashura's Edge party auras, Onimaru Blood-Quench Skillchain recovery surges, and enemy armor sundering.
souls.atAGlance: Warlord is a Great Katana tactical support Samurai that channels the cursed power of Onimaru into battlefield-wide momentum. You keep an aggressive sheathe-and-draw rhythm with Hagakure, build Ashura's Edge stacks to empower nearby allies, and close skillchains to trigger Onimaru Blood-Quench party recovery surges. In exchange for trading away a slice of personal attack and weaponskill output, Warlord turns every burst window into a decisive advantage for the entire group.
highlights: Open weapon choice, but requires a Great Katana for passive Accuracy, Store TP, Zanshin, Subtle Blow, and Iaijutsu support effects.

Hagakure (20s recast): enters Noto stance for 15s, turning your next Tachi weapon skill into an empowered Iaijutsu Draw-Slash with Save TP and Chainbound that inflicts Onimaru Sundering (Defense, Magic Defense, and Evasion Down for 15s).

Ashura's Edge (up to 3 stacks, 20s): projects a 15y party aura granting Subtle Blow, weaponskill damage, Accuracy/Magic Accuracy, and Regain; at 3 stacks, Great Katana swings restore HP and MP to nearby allies.
Onimaru Blood-Quench: closing a Skillchain amplifies Skillchain damage and restores HP, MP, and TP to party members within 15y.
Onimaru Tithe (25s recast, 15y, 12s): grants nearby allies immediate TP, boosted weaponskill damage, and lifesteal on melee and ranged hits while refreshing Ashura's Edge to 3 stacks.

Support tradeoff & job abilities: trades away personal Attack and weaponskill damage for group power; Hasso shares offensive stats within 15y, Meditate feeds TP to you and the party, Sekkanoki grants a 12s party critical boost, and Meikyo Shisui maximizes Ashura's Edge, resets Hagakure's recast, and strengthens Blood-Quench.

weaponConfig.summary: Required weapon: Main-hand a Great Katana. Your passive Accuracy, Store TP, Zanshin, Subtle Blow, Hasso aura, Noto draw-slash, and Ashura's Edge effects all require a Great Katana.

souls.equipmentCompatibility: Required weapon: Main-hand a Great Katana. Your passive Accuracy, Store TP, Zanshin, Subtle Blow, Hasso aura, Noto draw-slash, and Ashura's Edge effects all require a Great Katana.
souls.resourceSystem: Hagakure (20s recast): enters Noto stance for 15s, turning your next Tachi weapon skill into an empowered Iaijutsu Draw-Slash with Save TP and Chainbound that inflicts Onimaru Sundering (Defense, Magic Defense, and Evasion Down for 15s).
mechanics: Ashura's Edge: Up to 3 stacks lasting 20 seconds, projecting a 15-yalm party aura of Subtle Blow, weaponskill damage, Accuracy/Magic Accuracy, and Regain. At 3 stacks, Great Katana swings also restore HP and MP to nearby allies.

Hagakure (Iaijutsu Sundering Noto): 20-second recast; enters Noto stance for 15 seconds, turning your next Tachi weapon skill into an empowered Iaijutsu Draw-Slash that inflicts Onimaru Sundering (Defense, Magic Defense, and Evasion Down) for 15 seconds.
Onimaru Tithe: 25-second recast, 15-yalm party buff lasting 12 seconds; grants immediate TP, weaponskill damage, and lifesteal on physical hits while refreshing Ashura's Edge to 3 stacks.
Onimaru Blood-Quench: Closing a skillchain amplifies its damage and restores HP, MP, and TP to party members within 15 yalms.

Supportive Samurai JAs: Hasso shares offensive stats within 15 yalms; Meditate feeds TP to both you and your party; Sekkanoki grants a 12-second party critical bonus; Meikyo Shisui maximizes Ashura's Edge, removes Hagakure's cooldown, and doubles down on Blood-Quench.

Level progression: Great Katana passives, Iaijutsu draw-slash potency, and party aura strength grow as you level. Blade Bash and Sengikori unlock at Lv. 30, followed by Konzen-ittai and Shikikoyo at Lv. 50.

souls.lore: A shadowy master of forbidden duplication who surrounds their quarry with a fleeting retinue of striking mirror-selves.
souls.summary: Pure physical DPS shadow-clone commander (Lv. 10+, Katana): fields up to 5 fragile offensive shadow clones via Shadow Squadron: Ichi and Ni, sequencing varied squad commands through a Feint, Switch, and Cascade tactical cycle.
souls.atAGlance: Shinobi is a pure physical DPS shadow-clone commander that trades defensive decoys for relentless squad offense. Using Shadow Squadron, you field up to five fragile offensive shadow clones that mirror your appearance and independently assault your engaged target. Your core skill is keeping at least two clones striking the same enemy and sequencing distinct squad commands through the Feint → Switch → Cascade tactical cycle to unleash coordinated finishers.
highlights: Pure physical DPS specialization with full personal offensive focus and zero defensive shadow absorption from clones.
Passive progression strengthens STR, DEX, Katana skill, Attack, weaponskill damage, Double Attack, Store TP, and enmity reduction as you level.

Shadow Squadron (Ichi at Lv. 10, Ni at Lv. 37): summons 2 or 3 offensive shadow clones (up to 5 active, 25-30s lifetime, scaling fragile HP) that mirror your appearance and independently attack your engaged target.

Feint -> Switch -> Cascade tactical cycle: 2 distinct living clones landing verified hits within 6s establish Feint Ready (20s); sequence varied squad commands to advance through Switch and Cascade for a coordinated strike.

Zero-tool Ninjutsu squad commands: False Assault (Lv. 10, 12s recast), Mirror Step (Lv. 10, 16s recast), Crosscut (Lv. 10, 14s recast), Shadow Pin (Lv. 30, 18s recast), Thunder Relay (Lv. 50, 22s recast), and Final Mirage (Lv. 70, 45s recast).
Custom job abilities (Lv. 10+): Shadow Legion (90s recast, staggered full-squad burst) and Phantom Assault (30s recast, 8s accelerated clone attack cadence) feed directly into the tactical cycle.

weaponConfig.summary: Weapons: Equip Katana (ideally dual-wielded). Focus on Accuracy, Attack, STR, DEX, Haste, Store TP, and weaponskill damage to pair strong personal strikes with your squad's pressure.

souls.equipmentCompatibility: Weapons: Equip Katana (ideally dual-wielded). Focus on Accuracy, Attack, STR, DEX, Haste, Store TP, and weaponskill damage to pair strong personal strikes with your squad's pressure.
souls.resourceSystem: Pure physical DPS specialization with full personal offensive focus and zero defensive shadow absorption from clones.
mechanics: Offensive Shadow Squadron: Up to 5 active clones at once, each lasting 25–30 seconds with fragile HP that scales with level. They provide pure offense and zero defensive shadow absorption.

Feint → Switch → Cascade: Two distinct clones landing hits within 6 seconds establish Feint Ready. Each ready phase lasts about 20 seconds; advancing requires issuing a different successful squad command each step.
False Assault & Opening: 12-second recast; strikes as a feint and opens a 12-second Opening window that empowers your next different squad command.

Core squad commands: Mirror Step (Lv. 10, 16s recast; 10s alternating strike cadence scaling with squad size), Crosscut (Lv. 10, 14s recast; rapid single-target clone strikes), Shadow Pin (Lv. 30, 18s recast; 12s target lock and phase extension), Thunder Relay (Lv. 50, 22s recast; escalating relay for 2+ clones), and Final Mirage (Lv. 70, 45s recast; phase-consuming finisher).

Custom job abilities: Phantom Assault (30s recast, 8s duration; accelerates living clones' attack cadence) and Shadow Legion (90s recast, 12y range; staggered full-squad burst), both integrated into the tactical cycle.

Phase resets & HUD: Losing all clones, swapping targets, disengaging, dying, zoning, or letting a 20-second phase expire clears your cycle. The Soul HUD tracks living clones, Feint progress, active phase, Opening, and command readiness.

souls.lore: A phantom body-double of drifting ash and lantern smoke who bewilders foes with shifting decoys and vanishing silhouettes.
souls.summary: Decoy-detonating shadow and ninjutsu tank (Lv. 10+, Dual Katanas): casts Ninjutsu without consuming ninja tools, unlocks Utsusemi: Ichi and Ni from Lv. 10+, converts broken shadows into Kawarimi Ash and Shadow Smoke, and intercepts tankbusters with Migawari.
souls.atAGlance: Kagemusha is a dual-Katana shadow and ninjutsu tank that turns every broken decoy into fuel. Unlike Shinobi's offensive clones, Kagemusha treats Utsusemi shadows as a living defensive economy: each broken shadow generates TP, threat, Shadow Smoke debuffs on the attacker, and Kawarimi Ash. Spending Ash through Katana weapon skills rebuilds shadows and heals you, while Smoke Lotus, Kage Bunshin, Futae, and a transformed Mijin Gakure give you active threat, control, and tankbuster interception.
highlights: Passive tank progression strengthens Max HP, VIT, AGI, Defense, damage mitigation, Magic Evasion, Parry, Enmity, and enmity retention as you level.
Dual Katana & Ninjutsu Mastery: boosts Katana and Ninjutsu skill, Subtle Blow, and Ninjutsu cast speed while granting uninterruptible casting without consuming ninja tools.

Shadow Economy & Kawarimi Ash: Utsusemi: Ichi (3 shadows, 1.5s cast / 18s recast) and Ni (4 shadows, 1.2s cast / 28s recast) overwrite cleanly; broken shadows grant TP, enmity, Shadow Smoke (up to 4 stacks), and 1 Kawarimi Ash, while AoEs consume at most 2 shadows with partial bleedthrough.

Katana WS sustain & custom JAs: Katana weapon skills refresh Shadow Smoke and spend 3 Ash for +1 shadow and a self-heal; Kage Bunshin (45s recast) grants +3 shadows, 1 cleanse, and 6s magic mitigation; Smoke Lotus (30s recast, 8y) applies 4 stacks of Shadow Smoke, Slow, and +2 Ash.

Tank JAs: Yonin (15s recast) boosts Enmity and Magic Accuracy with emergency mitigation and Parry at 0 shadows; Futae (45s recast) grants instant Ninjutsu with heavy threat, a 2s Stun, and Magic Evasion Down; Mijin Gakure (120s recast) opens a 12s Migawari intercept negating massive hits while restoring HP and 4 shadows.

weaponConfig.summary: Strict weapons: Equip Katana in both Main and Sub. Using a single Katana, shield, or other offhand disables Kagemusha's core Ninjutsu, shadow, and tank bonuses.

souls.equipmentCompatibility: Strict weapons: Equip Katana in both Main and Sub. Using a single Katana, shield, or other offhand disables Kagemusha's core Ninjutsu, shadow, and tank bonuses.
souls.resourceSystem: Shadow Economy & Kawarimi Ash: Utsusemi: Ichi (3 shadows, 1.5s cast / 18s recast) and Ni (4 shadows, 1.2s cast / 28s recast) overwrite cleanly; broken shadows grant TP, enmity, Shadow Smoke (up to 4 stacks), and 1 Kawarimi Ash, while AoEs consume at most 2 shadows with partial bleedthrough.
mechanics: Utsusemi shadow economy: Ichi (3 shadows) and Ni (4 shadows) overwrite cleanly from Lv. 10. Breaking shadows awards TP, enmity, Shadow Smoke, and Kawarimi Ash; area attacks strip at most 2 shadows with partial bleedthrough.
Shadow Smoke: Stacks up to 4 times (15-second duration), weakening the attacker's Attack, Magic Attack, and Accuracy. Katana weapon skills refresh its duration.
Kawarimi Ash: Stacks up to 4 times (30-second duration) from broken shadows, Ninjutsu, and Smoke Lotus. Spending 3 stacks on a Katana weapon skill grants +1 shadow and a self-heal.

Smoke Lotus & Kage Bunshin: Smoke Lotus (30s recast, 8y) applies 4 stacks of Shadow Smoke, Slow, and +2 Ash. Kage Bunshin (45s recast) grants +3 shadows, cleanses 1 debuff, and adds 6 seconds of magic mitigation.

Yonin & Futae: Yonin (15s recast) boosts Enmity and Magic Accuracy, adding emergency damage mitigation and Parry at 0 shadows. Futae (45s recast) grants instant Ninjutsu with heavy threat, a 2-second Stun, and Magic Evasion Down.
Mijin Gakure (Migawari): 120-second recast; opens a 12-second Migawari intercept that negates massive hits while restoring HP and 4 shadows.

souls.lore: A vigilant watcher of the unseen clan who reads an enemy’s smallest tell and seals away looming danger with swift hand-signs.
souls.summary: Reactive tactical support Ninja: reads enemy telegraphs and answers them with zero-tool seals that disrupt a hostile spell or dampen a physical enemy technique.
souls.atAGlance: Fūin is a reactive tactical support Ninja that reads enemy telegraphs and shuts them down at the exact moment they happen. Severing Seal answers hostile spells—interrupting susceptible casts or blunting their direct magical damage if they still finish—while Blunting Seal dampens the impact of a physical enemy technique across your party. Rather than maintaining passive debuffs, Fūin protects the group through sharp observation and split-second timing.
highlights: Severing Seal (Lv. 10, 0 MP, no tools) can interrupt susceptible enemy spells on a full landing; if the spell still completes, it reduces that spell's direct magical damage.
Blunting Seal (Lv. 10, 0 MP, no tools) reduces the physical damage dealt by one telegraphed enemy technique across your party.
Both seals share a 20s recast (shortening to 18s at Lv. 50+) and incur only a 3s retry on a mismatched or expired telegraph.
Quick Read unlocks at Lv. 30 (45s recast, 8s duration) and halves your next valid seal's cast time; Signal Flare (10s recast) provides zero-tool single-target fire filler.

weaponConfig.summary: Weapons: Katana is Fūin's eligible weapon-skill family. The seal kit functions reliably with standard gear and any subjob.

souls.equipmentCompatibility: Weapons: Katana is Fūin's eligible weapon-skill family. The seal kit functions reliably with standard gear and any subjob.
souls.resourceSystem: Severing Seal: Unlocks at Lv. 10 (0 MP, no tools, 15-yalm range). Can interrupt susceptible enemy spells on a full landing; if the spell still finishes, it reduces that spell's direct damage.
mechanics: Severing Seal: Unlocks at Lv. 10 (0 MP, no tools, 15-yalm range). Can interrupt susceptible enemy spells on a full landing; if the spell still finishes, it reduces that spell's direct damage.
Blunting Seal: Unlocks at Lv. 10 (0 MP, no tools, 15-yalm range). Reduces the physical damage dealt by one telegraphed enemy technique to you and your allies.

Shared recast & retry forgiveness: Both seals share a 20-second recast (18 seconds from Lv. 50+). Casting into a mismatched, nonphysical (for Blunting), or already-finished telegraph triggers a brief 3-second retry instead of burning the full timer.
Quick Read (Lv. 30+): 45-second recast; lasts 8 seconds and halves your next valid seal's cast time from 0.5 seconds to 0.25 seconds.
Signal Flare: Unlocks at Lv. 10 (10-second recast, 0 MP, no tools); quick single-target fire filler spell.

Single-action binding: Seals bind to one specific target and its current action sequence. They cannot be banked for future attacks, and instant or scripted HP-change effects may not offer a sealable window.

souls.lore: A fearless spearhead who measures the open ground and surges across the battlefield in a devastating vaulted charge.
souls.summary: Polearm damage specialist whose long, unobstructed launch lanes deliver heavier Spineshatter Vault strikes and empower a Piercing Jump follow-through.
souls.atAGlance: Highlancer is a Polearm damage specialist that turns clear, long launch lanes into devastating opening strikes. Spineshatter Vault launches you across 4 to 12 yalms to strike your quarry; longer, unobstructed lanes beyond 7 yalms hit markedly harder. From Lv. 50 onward, landing a long Vault primes a 5-second follow-up window that empowers Piercing Jump against that same target. Mastering Highlancer means reading terrain, spacing your lanes cleanly, and knowing when a safe short Vault beats forcing a blocked line.
highlights: Spineshatter Vault unlocks at Lv. 10 (18s recast, 4 to 12 yalms): leaps to a safe landing spot near the enemy for a single Polearm strike.
Short lanes (4-7 yalms) deliver a reliable strike, while long lanes beyond 7 yalms hit substantially harder and scale further as you level.
Terrain-blocked lanes incur only a 3s retry without moving you or dealing damage.
From Lv. 50, landing a damaging long-lane Vault empowers your next Piercing Jump against that same enemy for 5s.

weaponConfig.summary: Weapon: Main-hand a Polearm. Spineshatter Vault, Piercing Jump's follow-up, and Highlancer's eligible weapon-skill family all require a Polearm.

souls.equipmentCompatibility: Weapon: Main-hand a Polearm. Spineshatter Vault, Piercing Jump's follow-up, and Highlancer's eligible weapon-skill family all require a Polearm.
souls.resourceSystem: Spineshatter Vault: Unlocks at Lv. 10 (18-second recast, 4 to 12 yalms). Short lanes (4–7 yalms) deliver a solid opening strike; long lanes (over 7–12 yalms) deal substantially higher damage that scales further as you level.
mechanics: Spineshatter Vault: Unlocks at Lv. 10 (18-second recast, 4 to 12 yalms). Short lanes (4–7 yalms) deliver a solid opening strike; long lanes (over 7–12 yalms) deal substantially higher damage that scales further as you level.
Blocked-lane forgiveness: Invalid or obstructed landing terrain incurs a 3-second recast without moving you or dealing damage.
Long-lane Jump follow-up (Lv. 50+): Damaging a surviving enemy with a long Vault empowers your next Piercing Jump against that same target for 5 seconds, growing stronger at higher levels.
Target binding: The 5-second follow-up belongs strictly to the enemy struck by your long Vault; jumping to a different enemy forfeits the bonus.
Jump & High Jump: Jump (60-second recast) delivers an aerial strike and pairs with the Lv. 50+ follow-up window; High Jump (120-second recast) provides a leaping strike that sheds enmity.
Level progression: Passive Polearm skill, STR, Accuracy, and Attack grow steadily as you level, alongside stronger long-lane Vaults and Lv. 50+ follow-up potency.

souls.lore: A proud lance-knight of the high crags who takes to the wind at the decisive heartbeat, descending with thunderous presence to command the field.
souls.summary: Grounded Polearm tank that opens with a ranged enmity challenge and braces through heavy direct hits with a tight timed guard without ever leaving melee.
souls.atAGlance: Drachenward is a Polearm tank built to lock down a single enemy's attention and brace through heavy direct hits without ever leaving melee range. Grounding Cry establishes strong opening threat from up to 15 yalms, while Skyward Guard creates a sharp 1.5-second defensive window to blunt a dangerous blow—granting a follow-up protective ward from Lv. 30 onward on a successful intercept. Unlike evasive jump styles, Drachenward stays grounded, targetable, and firmly at the top of the enmity list.
highlights: Grounding Cry (Lv. 10, 16s recast, 15y range) challenges a single enemy with heavy immediate threat.
Skyward Guard (Lv. 10, 20s recast) opens a 1.5s defensive window that sharply reduces one qualifying direct enemy hit, scaling stronger as you level.
Finishing Skyward Guard adds extra enmity to your original living target; from Lv. 30, a successful intercept also grants a 5s damage-absorbing ward.
Both Guard and its ward keep you targetable with your enmity intact, while periodic damage and scripted HP changes bypass both.

weaponConfig.summary: Required weapon: Main-hand a Polearm. Grounding Cry, Skyward Guard, and Drachenward's eligible weapon-skill family all require a Polearm.

souls.equipmentCompatibility: Required weapon: Main-hand a Polearm. Grounding Cry, Skyward Guard, and Drachenward's eligible weapon-skill family all require a Polearm.
souls.resourceSystem: Finishing Skyward Guard adds extra enmity to your original living target; from Lv. 30, a successful intercept also grants a 5s damage-absorbing ward.
mechanics: Grounding Cry: Unlocks at Lv. 10 (16-second recast, 15-yalm range); challenges a single enemy with strong cumulative and volatile enmity.
Skyward Guard: Unlocks at Lv. 10 (20-second recast); opens a 1.5-second window that heavily reduces one qualifying direct hit and adds enmity to your original living target upon landing.
Post-intercept ward (Lv. 30+): Successfully intercepting a qualifying blow with Skyward Guard grants a 5-second damage-absorbing ward whose strength grows as you level.

Eligible attacks & limits: Direct physical and ranged hits—plus qualifying direct magical and breath monster actions—can be intercepted. Damage-over-time effects and scripted HP changes bypass both Guard and the ward.
Grounded control: Both Skyward Guard and its ward leave you targetable and keep your hate intact, preventing boss movement or target resets.
Level progression: Passive Polearm skill, Max HP, and Enmity—along with Skyward Guard's mitigation and the Lv. 30+ ward's capacity—grow as you level, balanced by reduced personal damage output.

souls.lore: A dragon-bonded guardian whose kinship with a living wyvern channels soaring vitality and restorative breath to allies in peril.
souls.summary: Pure martial Dragon-Blood Polearm and Wyvern triage healer (Lv. 10+, Polearm): unlocks Call Wyvern, Jumps, Spirit Link, and Restoring Breath from Lv. 10+, builds Wyrmscale stacks into Max-HP-scaled party Healing Breaths, and commands Wyvern Crimson Triage on Polearm weapon skills.
souls.atAGlance: Wyvernheart is a martial Polearm and Wyvern triage healer whose recovery power scales directly from the Dragoon's own maximum HP alongside an active Wyvern. Polearm weapon skills, Jump, High Jump, and Spirit Link build Wyrmscale stacks while keeping allies stabilized, and Restoring Breath spends those stacks for sweeping party heals—adding a protective Dragonscale Stoneskin at full stacks. Instead of casting from the backline, Wyvernheart fights beside the party, weaving triage, cleanses, and Jump cooldown resets into every exchange.
highlights: Passive progression strengthens Max HP, VIT, MND, STR, Cure/Breath Potency, Subtle Blow, Polearm skill, Parry, and enmity reduction while fortifying your Wyvern with high durability and strong resistance to area magic and breath attacks.

Lv. 10+ kit & Polearm Triage: unlocks Call Wyvern (15s recast, usable in combat at full HP), Jump, High Jump, Spirit Link, and Restoring Breath at Lv. 10+ (Super Jump at Lv. 50+); Polearm weapon skills trigger Wyvern Crimson Triage on the lowest-HP ally (converting overheal to Stoneskin) and grant 1 Wyrmscale (max 3).

Jump directives & Spirit Link: Jump (20s recast) grants TP, +1 Wyrmscale, dual-target Regen, and 1 cleanse; High Jump (35s recast) grants +1 Wyrmscale, a 15y 2-debuff party cleanse, and Stoneskin; Spirit Link (15s recast, no self-HP drain) heals a single ally with 2 cleanses, restores Wyvern HP, and adds +1 Wyrmscale.

Restoring Breath & Super Jump: Restoring Breath (20s recast) spends 0-3 Wyrmscale for a Max-HP-scaled party heal (adding a 12s Dragonscale Stoneskin at 3 stacks); Super Jump (Lv. 50+, 75s recast) wipes enmity, hides your Wyvern for 8s, and grants 3 Wyrmscale; Spirit Surge halves Jump recasts and adds 2 Wyrmscale.

Wyrmblood Pulse (45s recast, 15y AoE) heals the party, cleanses 2 debuffs, and resets Jump and High Jump; Dragonscale Sanctuary (75s recast, 15y AoE, 15s) grants Stoneskin, knockback immunity, and a shared mitigation and Magic Evasion ward.

weaponConfig.summary: Required weapon: Main-hand a Polearm. Your Crimson Triage healing procs and weapon-skill Wyrmscale generation require a Polearm.

souls.equipmentCompatibility: Required weapon: Main-hand a Polearm. Your Crimson Triage healing procs and weapon-skill Wyrmscale generation require a Polearm.
souls.resourceSystem: Passive progression strengthens Max HP, VIT, MND, STR, Cure/Breath Potency, Subtle Blow, Polearm skill, Parry, and enmity reduction while fortifying your Wyvern with high durability and strong resistance to area magic and breath attacks.
mechanics: Wyrmscale: Stacks up to 3 times (30-second duration), built via Polearm weapon skills, Jump, High Jump, Spirit Link, Spirit Surge, and Super Jump.
Crimson Triage: Triggered by Polearm weapon skills; commands your Wyvern to heal the most injured ally within 15 yalms based on your Max HP, turning overheal into Stoneskin.
Restoring Breath: 20-second recast; consumes up to 3 Wyrmscale for a scaling party heal based on your Max HP, adding a 12-second Dragonscale Stoneskin at 3 stacks.

Distinct Jump directives: Jump (20s recast) grants TP, +1 Wyrmscale, dual-target Regen, and 1 cleanse; High Jump (35s recast) grants +1 Wyrmscale, a 15-yalm 2-debuff party cleanse, and Stoneskin; Super Jump (Lv. 50+, 75s recast) wipes enmity, shelters your Wyvern for 8 seconds, and grants 3 Wyrmscale.
Spirit Link: 15-second recast, zero self-HP cost; heals a single ally, removes 2 debuffs, restores Wyvern HP, and adds +1 Wyrmscale.

Wyrmblood Pulse & Dragonscale Sanctuary: Wyrmblood Pulse (45s recast, 15y) heals the party, cleanses 2 debuffs, and resets Jump/High Jump. Dragonscale Sanctuary (75s recast, 15y, 15s) grants Stoneskin, knockback immunity, and a shared mitigation/Magic Evasion ward.

souls.lore: An avatar-channeler attuned to the shifting elements who invokes celestial fury when the winds of elemental allegiance align.
souls.summary: Single-target elemental damage Summoner that commits an avatar's element to one quarry and exploits the enemy's weakest elemental resistance.
souls.atAGlance: Eidolarch is a single-target elemental damage Summoner built around exploiting each enemy's weakest elemental resistance. Rather than juggling every avatar at once from the start, you summon a focused elemental partner, mark your quarry with Challenge Aspect, and unleash a matching single-target Rage pact during the Challenge window. Matching the enemy's least-resisted element rewards you with empowered pact damage, while an unmatched element still deals baseline damage without the bonus.
highlights: Lv. 10: summon Carbuncle (Light) or Ifrit (Fire) for 5 MP and pair Challenge Aspect (20s recast) with its matching single-target Elemental Pact (18s shared recast).
Lv. 30: attune two additional Prime avatars from Shiva, Garuda, Titan, Leviathan, and Ramuh; Lv. 50: all seven avatars become available.
Challenge Aspect opens a 12s window (15s from Lv. 70+) that empowers matching pacts against the enemy's least-resisted element, growing stronger as you level.

weaponConfig.summary: Weapons: Staff and Club are Eidolarch's eligible weapon-skill families. The core avatar-and-pact loop works smoothly with standard gear and any subjob.

souls.equipmentCompatibility: Weapons: Staff and Club are Eidolarch's eligible weapon-skill families. The core avatar-and-pact loop works smoothly with standard gear and any subjob.
souls.resourceSystem: Lv. 10: summon Carbuncle (Light) or Ifrit (Fire) for 5 MP and pair Challenge Aspect (20s recast) with its matching single-target Elemental Pact (18s shared recast).
mechanics: Avatar progression: Carbuncle and Ifrit unlock at Lv. 10; two selectable Prime attunements unlock at Lv. 30; all seven avatars (Carbuncle, Ifrit, Shiva, Garuda, Titan, Leviathan, Ramuh) unlock at Lv. 50.

Challenge Aspect: 20-second recast; opens a 12-second window (extending to 15 seconds at Lv. 70+) that empowers a matching elemental pact against that target when its element matches the target's least-resisted rank.
Elemental resistance check: When the pact resolves, the enemy's eight elemental resistance ranks are compared. Even a tie for the lowest resistance qualifies for the Challenge bonus.
Target & avatar binding: The challenged enemy, its active spawn, and the summoned avatar must remain matched when the pact lands.
Shared pact recast: Elemental Rage pacts share an 18-second recast and have MP costs that scale with level.
Attunement persistence: Your Lv. 30–49 Prime selections are saved for level sync; changing a slot may dismiss its previous avatar.

souls.lore: A serene pact-keeper who calls down starlit avatars to weave tranquil sanctuaries of comfort and celestial grace.
souls.summary: Astral Avatar conduit, sanctuary, and ward-reset healer (Lv. 10+): projects a 15y Celestial Sanctuary aura from your active Avatar, shortens Blood Pact: Ward to 12s (6s in Apogee, 5s in Astral Flow), and pulses Starlight Mend on Wards and Staff/Club weapon skills.
souls.atAGlance: Celestial is an Avatar-anchored Summoner healer that turns your summoned Avatar into a radiant beacon of protection and recovery. Whenever an Avatar is active, it projects Celestial Sanctuary, bathing nearby allies in continuous Regen, Refresh, and damage mitigation. Shortened Blood Pact: Ward recasts and eligible Staff or Club weapon skills pulse Starlight Mend across the party, while Celestial Convergence, Astral Benediction, and an enhanced Elemental Siphon give you responsive group healing, cleansing, Reraise, and MP recovery.
highlights: Passive progression strengthens Max HP, Max MP, MND, CHR, Cure and Ward Potency, Fast Cast, Refresh, and enmity reduction as you level while eliminating Avatar perpetuation cost.
Astral Avatar Resonance: your active Avatar projects Celestial Sanctuary (15y radius), granting continuous scaling HP Regen, MP Refresh, and damage mitigation.

Ward-Loop & Starlight Mend: Blood Pact: Ward runs on a flat 12s recast (6s in Apogee, 5s in Astral Flow); both Wards and Staff/Club weapon skills heavily heal your Avatar and pulse a party heal within 15y.
Job ability enhancements: Elemental Siphon (20s recast) restores substantial MP and heals the party without dismissing your Avatar; Astral Flow drops Ward recast to 5s and adds party Stoneskin.

Astral Benediction (22s recast, 15y AoE) delivers a large party heal, cleanses up to 3 debuffs, and grants Reraise III; Celestial Convergence (25s recast, 15y AoE, 12s) boosts party damage mitigation and Magic Evasion while restoring party MP on every Ward or Staff/Club weapon skill.

weaponConfig.summary: Avatar uptime: Keep an Avatar summoned at all times. Celestial eliminates Avatar perpetuation cost, and losing your Avatar shuts down Celestial Sanctuary and your Ward-driven healing loop.

souls.equipmentCompatibility: Avatar uptime: Keep an Avatar summoned at all times. Celestial eliminates Avatar perpetuation cost, and losing your Avatar shuts down Celestial Sanctuary and your Ward-driven healing loop.
souls.resourceSystem: Passive progression strengthens Max HP, Max MP, MND, CHR, Cure and Ward Potency, Fast Cast, Refresh, and enmity reduction as you level while eliminating Avatar perpetuation cost.
mechanics: Celestial Sanctuary: Projected in a 15-yalm radius from your active Avatar, providing continuous HP Regen, MP Refresh, and Damage Taken reduction that scale as you level.

Ward-Loop & Starlight Mend: Blood Pact: Ward runs on a flat 12-second recast (6 seconds in Apogee, 5 seconds in Astral Flow). Both Wards and Staff/Club weapon skills trigger Starlight Mend, heavily healing your Avatar and pulsing a party heal within 15 yalms. (Blood Pact: Rage is unaffected.)
Celestial Convergence: 25-second recast, 15-yalm AoE, 12-second duration; grants party damage mitigation and Magic Evasion while causing each Ward or Staff/Club weapon skill to restore party MP.
Astral Benediction: 22-second recast, 15-yalm AoE; delivers a large party heal, removes up to 3 debuffs, and applies Reraise III.

Elemental Siphon & Astral Flow: Elemental Siphon (20-second recast) restores substantial MP and heals the party without dismissing your Avatar. Astral Flow drops Ward recast to 5 seconds and adds a party Stoneskin barrier.

Level progression: Passive Max HP/MP, MND, CHR, Cure/Ward Potency, Fast Cast, Refresh, enmity reduction, and Celestial Sanctuary's Regen/Refresh strength all grow as you level, with Avatar perpetuation cost eliminated.

souls.lore: A voice of the astral accords who announces an avatar’s elemental chorus, uniting allies in a shared symphony of planar power.
souls.summary: Invite temporary avatar envoys to align your party around a chosen element, empowering one matching elemental strike per covered ally.
souls.atAGlance: Accordant is an elemental support Soul that calls upon temporary avatar envoys and casts Astral Accord to empower one matching elemental hit per eligible party member. Your main decisions are choosing the element your party can best exploit, keeping your envoy positioned and available, and timing Accord when allies are ready to unleash their burst. Rather than maintaining a permanent damage aura, Accordant excels at sharp, coordinated elemental strike windows.
highlights: Lv. 10: Invite Carbuncle (Light) or Ifrit (Fire), cast Astral Accord, and follow through with your envoy's elemental response.
Astral Accord snapshots party members within 15y, draws a modest share of maximum MP, and recasts every 30s.
Each covered member can claim one matching direct elemental hit per window (master and pet share one claim), with bonus potency scaling up as you level.
Shiva and Garuda unlock at Lv. 30; Titan, Leviathan, and Ramuh unlock at Lv. 50. The Accord window extends from 8s to 10s at Lv. 70.

weaponConfig.summary: Weapons: Staff and Club are the eligible weapon-skill families. The opening support loop requires no weapon-skill talent investment and works with any subjob.

souls.equipmentCompatibility: Weapons: Staff and Club are the eligible weapon-skill families. The opening support loop requires no weapon-skill talent investment and works with any subjob.
souls.resourceSystem: Each covered member can claim one matching direct elemental hit per window (master and pet share one claim), with bonus potency scaling up as you level.
mechanics: Envoy progression: Carbuncle (Light) and Ifrit (Fire) unlock at Lv. 10; Shiva (Ice) and Garuda (Wind) join at Lv. 30; Titan (Earth), Leviathan (Water), and Ramuh (Lightning) join at Lv. 50.
Scaling Accord: Astral Accord's elemental damage bonus grows stronger as you level, and its active window lengthens from 8 seconds to 10 seconds at Lv. 70.
Snapshotting recipients: Party members must be within 15 yalms when Astral Accord is cast and remain in the party and battle area. Once covered, they are free to move away from you.
Claim limits: Each eligible party member can claim one matching hit per Accord; a master and their pet share a single claim.

Qualifying hits: Only direct matching elemental spells, elemental weapon skills, and damaging pet abilities consume a claim. Damage-over-time ticks and skillchains do not spend a claim, and separate Soul burst effects do not stack with Accord's bonus.

Refreshing and overlap: Refreshing the same element does not restore already-spent claims, and when multiple Accords overlap, the stronger one takes precedence. Losing, dismissing, or replacing your envoy ends the current Accord.

souls.lore: A calculating student of bestial lore who curates an arsenal of stolen monster arts to answer any foe’s defenses.
souls.summary: Read a single enemy's defenses and answer with the monster technique it resists least.
souls.atAGlance: Assimilator is a single-target Blue Magic damage Soul that uses Assess Prey to read a foe's defenses and identify which damage categories it resists least. Your monster-spell arsenal covers blunt, slashing, and piercing physical attacks from Lv. 10, then expands into elemental options at higher levels. Landing a matching Blue Magic spell during the eight-second assessment window grants bonus damage after resistance checks, rewarding adaptable spell selection over a rigid one-button rotation.
highlights: Passive Progression: Accuracy, Magic Accuracy, Magic Attack, and INT all grow steadily as you level.
Assess Prey (12s recast, 15y) identifies every tied least-resistant damage category available at your level for 8s.
Matching direct Blue Magic spells gain bonus damage after resistance checks, scaling stronger as you level.

souls.lore: A twin-bladed alchemist of azure essence whose fluid strikes and esoteric chants ripple outward in waves of renewal.
souls.summary: Dual-wielding Blue Mage combat healer (Lv. 10+): splashes healing Blue Magic across the party, builds Azure Catalyst on melee hits and weapon skills, and siphons HP and MP for allies through Osmotic Conduit.
souls.atAGlance: Magus is a dual-wielding Blue Mage combat healer that weaves melee strikes with restorative Blue Magic to sustain the party. Qualifying weapon attacks build Azure Catalyst stacks that erupt into Azure Mending Wave party heals, while your healing Blue Magic splashes a large share of its recovery to nearby allies. Osmotic Conduit, White Wind Surge, and a shortened Diffusion recast round out a proactive frontline healer kit—Magus is built to fight in melee while mending, not to stand idle in the backline.
highlights: Passive Progression: Unlocks Dual Wield at Lv. 10 and strengthens Dual Wield delay reduction, Max HP, Max MP, MND, INT, Cure Potency, Fast Cast, Refresh, Sword/Club skill, and enmity reduction as you level, with uninterruptible casting during Diffusion and Unbridled Learning.
Azure Mending & AoE Diffusion: Qualifying healing Blue Magic automatically splashes a large share of its recovery to all party members within 15y.

Sanguine Catalyst: Qualifying dual-wield hits stack Azure Catalyst (up to 5 stacks); reaching 5 stacks or landing an eligible Sword/Club weapon skill unleashes Azure Mending Wave, restoring party HP and MP within 15y.
JA Enhancements: Diffusion is shortened to a 20s recast for frequent group buffing, and Azure Lore greatly amplifies Azure Mending Wave healing.

White Wind Surge (20s recast, 15y AoE) delivers a potent party heal, 2-debuff cleanse, and Stoneskin; Osmotic Conduit (25s recast, 12s) grants party magic damage reduction and turns melee swings into party HP and MP siphons.

Role tradeoff: Magus's personal offensive damage is tuned down in exchange for frontline healing output. Your swings exist to power Catalyst waves and Conduit siphons, not to top damage meters.

souls.lore: An Immortal sentinel who tempers body and spirit with assimilated monstrous resilience, adapting their carapace to every peril.
souls.summary: Monster-forged Blue Mage dual-wield tank (Lv. 10+): pairs early Dual Wield and uninterruptible spellcasting with Chitin Carapace mitigation and reactive physical-to-defensive Blue Magic weaving.
souls.atAGlance: Chrysalis is a monster-core Blue Mage tank that dual-wields on the frontline and weaves physical and defensive Blue Magic to hold enmity and absorb heavy blows. Designated physical Blue spells build Chitin Carapace stacks for layered Defense and damage mitigation; at three or more stacks, your defensive Blue Magic gains enhanced potency and restores MP. Eligible Sword or Club weapon skills trigger Azure Surge, turning your next Blue spell into an instant, MP-free cast with a close-range enmity pulse.
highlights: Passive Progression: Unlocks Dual Wield at Lv. 10 and scales Max HP, VIT, STR, MND, Defense, damage mitigation, Enmity, Enmity Retention, Sword/Club/Blue Magic skill, Parry, Fast Cast, and uninterruptible spellcasting as you level.

Monster-Core Carapace: Designated physical Blue Magic (Head Butt, Sudden Lunge, Bludgeon, Smite of Rage, Heavy Strike, Goblin Rush) costs less MP, generates heavy volatile enmity, and stacks Chitin Carapace (max 5, 15s) for layered Defense and damage mitigation; at 3+ stacks, defensive Blue Magic gains boosted potency and restores MP.
Azure Assimilation: Eligible Sword or Club weapon skills grant Azure Surge (6s), making your next Blue Magic spell instant-cast, 0 MP, and accompanied by an 8y volatile enmity pulse.

Tradeoff & JA Enhancements: Trades personal Attack, Ranged Attack, and Weapon Skill Damage for tank durability; enhances Burst Affinity (heavy volatile enmity and Magic Attack Down), Chain Affinity (3s Stun and barrier), and Azure Lore (stronger mitigation, enmity, and reduced Blue Magic MP costs).

Behemoth Roar (25s recast, 8y) opens with stun, enemy offense debuffs, and instant 5-stack Carapace; Diamond Shell (30s recast, 10s) provides mitigation, Stoneskin, knockback immunity, and threat from incoming damage.

Affinity & Azure Lore enhancements: Burst Affinity adds heavy volatile enmity and Magic Attack Down; Chain Affinity adds a 3-second Stun and a protective barrier; Azure Lore boosts damage mitigation and enmity while cutting Blue Magic MP costs.

souls.lore: A relentless gunslinger of sea-salt and smoke who unleashes disciplined volleys of blazing shot across the deck.
souls.summary: Pure single-target Gun damage Corsair (Lv. 10+): replaces party rolls with Deadeye Chamber, primes Powder Mark via Quick Draw for Marksmanship weapon-skill detonations, and provides full Bullet and Card recycle with no self-healing.
souls.atAGlance: Flintlock is a pure single-target Gun damage Corsair that trades away party rolls and self-healing for relentless ranged burst. Your core loop revolves around keeping Deadeye Chamber active on yourself, priming targets with Powder Mark via Quick Draw, and detonating that mark with a Marksmanship weapon skill for bonus fire damage and a TP refund. Hair Trigger opens an aggressive offense-first burst window, while Broadside Salvo delivers a heavy ranged strike alongside bonus TP and a Quick Draw recharge.
highlights: Passive Progression (Gun required): Strengthens Ranged Attack, Magic Attack, Snapshot, Rapid Shot, Ranged Critical Rate, Marksmanship skill, and enmity reduction as you level, with full Bullet and Card recycle.
Deadeye Chamber (Phantom Roll, 15s recast, self-only): Grants a 30s personal buff to Ranged/Magic Weapon Skill Damage (scaling with level) and Ranged Critical Damage.
Powder Mark (Quick Draw, 2 charges, 10s recharge): Marks a single target for 10s; detonating your mark with a Gun-equipped Marksmanship weapon skill deals bonus fire damage and refunds TP.

Hair Trigger (30s recast, 10s) boosts Triple Shot, Snapshot, and Weapon Skill Damage at the cost of Defense; Broadside Salvo (22s recast, 20y) fires a heavy single-target ranged shot that grants bonus TP and restores 1 Quick Draw charge.

souls.lore: A daring fortune-weaver of ivory dice and phantom cards who steadies the crew’s luck while flirting with audacious wagers.
souls.summary: Pure party-support Corsair (Lv. 10+): maintains up to 3 active rolls with Safe Standing floor protection, Overdrive jackpots on Lucky and XI, Card Counting Quick Draw steering, and full Bullet and Card recycle.
souls.atAGlance: Gambler is a pure party-support Corsair that trades personal damage for potent Phantom Roll buffs and reliable party cooldown recovery. High-Roller Stakes gives non-bust rolls a strong Safe Standing baseline so moderate dice totals still deliver high value, while landing a Lucky number or XI triggers Overdrive potency and bonus party resources. With Card Counting, Snake Eye, House Advantage, and Fold, you actively steer the odds—and if you Bust, the penalty lands on you through HP/TP pressure and House Debt rather than wiping away the party's active buffs.
highlights: Passive Progression: Supports 3 simultaneous Phantom Rolls with extended roll duration and scales Max HP, Max MP, AGI, CHR, Roll Potency, and enmity reduction as you level, plus full Bullet and Card recycle.
High-Roller Stakes: Non-bust rolls (1–10) enjoy a strong Safe Standing baseline, while Lucky and XI trigger Overdrive potency, clear Bust, and pulse TP and MP to party members within 15y.

Card Counting & Cooldown Recovery: Random Deal (35s recast, 15y) shaves time off standard party job abilities (excluding one-hour abilities, Wild Card, Random Deal, and Dead Man's Hand); Quick Draw steers your next Double-Up, applies Expose, and trims party recasts.

House Advantage (30s recast, 15y) forces an XI roll while buffing nearby allies' offense; Dead Man's Hand (35s recast, 20y) strips up to 2 enemy buffs, inflicts Breach, shaves party job-ability recasts, and awards bonus party TP on Lucky/XI.
